## Conclusions
- **Fine-tuning is the big lever: +16.0 points** on RefCOCOg-LPCVC (71.38 → 87.34, paired CI +14.2..+17.6),
  consistent on every fold (86.5–88.3 after vs. 69.7–73.5 before). That is far more than any model swap
  (≤ +1 for S3/S4) or zero-shot teacher (≤ +2.9, exp 009) could give.
- **Recipe (fixed before the run):** 15,905 RefCOCO/RefCOCO+/RefCOCOg train images (no reserved image), 5 epochs,
  256 images × 2 captions per step (310 steps), AdamW lr 1e-5, wd 0.1, 10% warmup + cosine, bf16, frozen
  logit scale, random horizontal flip only. Training ran through the deployment wrappers. Wall time ~22 min on the 4080 SUPER.
- **Most of the gain arrives in epoch 1** (85.2); epochs 2–5 add ~2 more points and the curve is flat after
  epoch 4. We report the last epoch; the curve was not used for selection.
- **LPCVC sample: 88.91 → 91.37 (+2.5).** That is in the right direction but within noise on 56 images (CI ±6), and
  the sample is near its ceiling. **Caveat for the report:** the validation folds come from the same
  annotation family as the training data (different images, same caption style), so +16 is probably an
  over-estimate of the gain on the hidden LPCVC test set. The LPCVC sample captions are themselves RefCOCO-like
  ("the blue car", "the purple car": telling apart same-category objects), which is why we use this data. The
  cross-source ablation (train on RefCOCO/RefCOCO+ only, test on the RefCOCOg-derived folds) measures how much of the gain carries across caption styles.
- **Architecture unchanged**, so latency should be identical to exp 004 (17.7 ms); verified on the S22 in exp 011.
- **Next:** distillation with the same recipe (012), cross-source ablation, WiSE-FT blending, then apply the
  recipe to S0.
